# A test's locals are its own. The lowerers bound the component instance to a
# hardcoded `c` in *every* test, whether the test declared one or not, so a
# local of that name was a redeclaration.
#
# It failed in the worst way it could. On html the emitted module no longer
# parsed, so the page never ran and all the runner could say was that the
# agent had not connected within 15s -- nothing about a name, a test, or a
# line. On the Go targets it was at least a compiler error, but on a file
# nobody had written.
#
# The name is the declaration's now: bound where a test declares a component
# parameter, and nowhere else.

sngl test --platform none app.sngl
stdout '3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform bubbletea app.sngl
stdout '3 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

output {
    none { html }
    go { bubbletea }
}

struct Counter {
    n int = 0

    func bump() Counter {
        var next = this
        next.n = this.n + 1
        return next
    }
}

component main node {
    var count Counter

    func tick() {
        count = count.bump()
    }

    text(value="{count.n}")
}

// `c` is this test's own local, not the component the runner builds.
func testALocalNamedC(t Test) {
    var c = Counter{}
    c = c.bump().bump()
    t.assert(c.n == 2)
}

// So is `t`'s neighbour in a test that never asks for a component at all.
func testNoComponentParam(t Test) {
    t.assert(Counter{}.bump().n == 1)
}

// And a test that does ask binds the name it asked under.
func testComponentParamIsBound(t Test, screen main) {
    screen.tick()
    t.assert(screen.count.n == 1)
}

window {
    main
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/_/1 --

      "Passed": true

      "Desc": "NoComponentParam",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
